previousRound.outcome: All five answered. The lock is bounded (`-w installLockWaitSeconds`). `/usr/bin/flock` is declared in every place I named and three I did not: the Dockerfile's apt line, the image's toolchain capability summary, `toolchain()`'s own list, the capability test stubs, the image test's expected detail, the build-time `flock --version` step, and the third-party notices. The two rate sentences are corrected — `plugins.go` now says several of the six and records the four runs as 3, 4, 2 and 3, and points at the chalk/lodash probe where its rate is scoped; `plugins_test.go`'s invented rates are gone — and the correct `docs/kubernetes.md` paragraph was left alone, which I checked rather than assumed. The cache default is dropped for `cache="$BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR"`, so `set -u` aborts rather than a fallback silencing it. And `bunInstallArgs` now skips without `/usr/bin/flock` and pins `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` under `t.TempDir()`, so the suite no longer locks the issue's shared cache when it runs in a pod.

keyFindings.description: The wait is a constant correct only at the daemon's defaults, and its comment presents the arithmetic as unconditional. `installLockWaitSeconds = 120` is sized against worker_boot_timeout_seconds 120 x worker_boot_registration_deadline_intervals 3 = 360, and two waits of 120 leave 120 for the install and the agent's start. Both are operator-settable. At a halved boot timeout the deadline is 180 and two waits are 240, so the bound cannot fire before the deadline retires the role — which is the failure the bound exists to prevent, arriving silently by arithmetic on a tuned deployment. TestTheInstallLockWaitIsABoundTwoOfWhichFitTheRegistrationDeadline reads the deadline from `config.LoadForValidation` of a minimal file, so it catches a change to the *defaults* and cannot catch an operator who sets either value, which is the case that matters. The architect has ruled the derivation rather than a documented conditional, and reports the values reachable: `sandbox.Options.BootTimeout` is already set from `cfg.WorkerBootTimeout`, and the intervals need one new field beside it from the same config, derived through `runtime.RegistrationDeadline` so it survives the deadline ceasing to be a plain product. Two things to carry with it, both measured here rather than assumed: a derived wait can round to zero and `-w 0` is byte-for-byte `-n` — against a held lock `-w 0` returned exit 1 after 0s where `-w 3` waited its full 3s — so it must be floored at a positive value, and the assertion has to become a property over several configurations including a deliberately small one rather than the single-constant check it is today. The comment should argue the proportion before stating the sum: a third of the deadline is right because it scales, not because it is 120.

serialisationTest.mutation: With `installLockWaitSeconds = 0` and nothing else changed: TestAnInstallingLaunchWrapsTheAgentArgvInTheInstallScript PASSES (its assertion is built with fmt.Sprintf over the constant, so it follows the mutation and cannot see it), TestTwoRenderedInstallsSerialiseOnTheSharedBunCache FAILS ('the log is not two completed installs: [start a, end a]' — at -w 0 the second install never gets the lock and never runs bun), and TestTheInstallLockWaitIsABoundTwoOfWhichFitTheRegistrationDeadline FAILS naming the non-positive bound. Restored, all three pass (1.234s), workspace unchanged. That is the claim made and it is the direction claimed: the new tests catch what the old ones could not.
threePoints: The substitution leaves the lock in the text under test: installLockProbe replaces `/usr/local/bin/bun` alone, so `/usr/bin/flock -w N -- "$cache"` is in what runs; the control strips the lock explicitly, from flock's own path through the locked directory so it survives the wait being respelled, and t.Fatal's if that prefix is not there.

The vacuity guard fails rather than skips: a control that never interleaves in five attempts is a t.Fatalf saying the locked run passed vacuously, not a quiet green. Five attempts is a bound, not a loop that can report success on the fifth — it returns on the first interleave and falls through to the Fatalf.

The harness is honest about what it ignores: exit codes, because the contract check's node has no package.json, so the proof is the log alone — two appends per process to a file opened in append mode.

ciShapes: The default check-runs page is 30 and these commits carry 25 to 39; read with per_page=100 and --paginate or required names fall off it.
A push that carries code and handoff together leaves the code commit with no run of its own; the head that merges is the one GitHub judged.

A required workflow can have many runs on one head — pr-title has had sixteen on one — because it fires on every pull-request edit; the newest decides, and a cancelled run superseded by a later success leaves no verdict rather than a red one.
The non-required `dispatch` lane has rarely settled on this branch, and envoy-smoke was red at an earlier head on a live envoy-infra listener step this diff cannot reach.
